text:
Leo (sales): FYI — AuroraHealth just hit sustained queueing on west1 during their interactive demo. They want a short burst to avoid a failed customer presentation in 2h.
Anya (support): Do we have the request details? start/end time, API key, model, and how many GPUs they want?
Maria (aurora-cust): Start ~2:30pm PST, for ~90 minutes. We need lower latency for `gpt-medium-16k` clients — currently responses are timing out for live sessions. Ideally +40 GPUs for 2 hours. Our traffic pattern is 60->140 concurrent streams.
Tomas (eng-sre): Copy. Looking at CapacityBot: 
CapacityBot: cluster-west1-gpu: 95% util; pending-queue-length: 320 requests; admission-window dropped 28% in last 10m. Autoscaler hitting region quota ceilings.
Tomas (eng-sre): So two things: autoscaler can't allocate because cloud quota and physical rack capacity in west1 are saturated. Admission control is enforcing per-tenant in-flight request caps which is why clients are getting 429/queueing.
Anya (support): Can we do a temporary override? Sales wants us to "make it work" for the demo.
Tomas (eng-sre): We can propose a short-lived soft override that increases this customer's per-tenant admission cap and grants them a burst reservation, but it requires: 1) a capacity-team approval to lift quota (if physical GPUs need provisioning) or 2) routing to another region (west2) or 3) model fallback to a smaller instance class. Each has tradeoffs: cost, latency, and data residency.
Leo (sales): Customer prefers west1 due to lower RTT. West2 adds ~40ms which might break demo. They accept a model fallback if quality holds.
Tomas (eng-sre): Practical plan: 
- Option A (fastest): Temporary per-tenant admission uplift + burst tokens for 2 hours (no new GPUs). This only helps if queuing is admission-driven and there's spare headroom on existing hosts. Risk: increases tail latency for others. Requires ops sign-off.
- Option B: Canary route 30% of sessions to west2 and enable cache-warmup for key prefixes. More work but safer.
- Option C: Force-fallback to `gpt-small-8k` for non-critical streams. Lowers token cost ~2.4x.
Anya (support): What does it take to do A? commands or config?
Tomas (eng-sre): We can toggle a customer-level override flag via infra API: 
```
POST /internal/quota/override
{ "customer_id": "aurora-001", "admission_limit": 400, "burst_capacity": 40, "expires_at": "2026-03-15T22:30:00Z" }
```
This will update admission controller and credit burst tokens. Need 2 approvals: SRE lead + finance for cost exposure. Also we should set a hard kill at expiry.
Leo (sales): Estimate the incremental cost for 2h? Need to tell customer ASAP.
Tomas (eng-sre): Rough calc: 40 GPUs * 2h * $2.70/hr = ~$216. Add buffer for model tokens and routing ~ $300 total.
Nina (finance): Pinged — can approve up to $500 for demo-related bursts if sales confirms customer will cover any overage.
Anya (support): Customer?
Maria (aurora-cust): We'll cover overage for this demo. Please proceed if you can guarantee no cross-tenant degradation.
Tomas (eng-sre): I recommend Option A + strict expiry + 10m canary ramp: start with 15% traffic uplift for 10m, monitor p95/p99 and queue length, then go to full burst if stable. I'll run the override and the canary script.
Anya (support): I'm filing the temporary exception ticket now and will include the cost approval.
Anya (support): Ticket: `EXC-20260315-aurora-burst` created — includes customer acceptance and finance OK.
CapacityBot: quota-override-request logged: EXC-20260315-aurora-burst, approvers: tomas, nina.
Tomas (eng-sre): I'll deploy the canary at T+30min and watch. If anything crosses thresholds (p99 > 2s or queue > 400), I roll back immediately.
Leo (sales): Thanks team — I'll message Aurora to confirm the schedule and cost.
Maria (aurora-cust): Thanks all, much appreciated.
Nina (finance): Approved. Please tag billing code `AUR-DEMO-23` for this override.
Tomas (eng-sre): Action items: 
- Anya: attach customer API key & SLA note to EXC ticket
- Nina: add billing code to ticket
- Leo: confirm exact start time
- Me: toggle override + run canary and watch metrics (p95/p99, queue, host CPU/GPU).
Anya (support): Will do.
Tomas (eng-sre): Updating thread when the override is applied.
Anya (support): Marking as in-progress.
Tomas (eng-sre): OVERRIDE APPLIED (1788432410) — admission_limit=400, burst_capacity=40, expires=2026-03-15T22:30:00Z. Canary ramp started at 15%. Monitoring.
Leo (sales): Noted.
Tomas (eng-sre): Canary stable after 12m. Ramped to 100% at 1788432405.
Anya (support): Closing once expiry completes and post-mortem note added.
Maria (aurora-cust): Demo succeeded. Great work :tada:
Tomas (eng-sre): Rolling back at expiry window now. All metrics back to baseline.
Anya (support): EXC ticket updated with outcome and cost summary.
Nina (finance): Invoice prep note added.
Leo (sales): Thanks everyone — saved demo.
